questions.prompt: Tell me about a time one of your Java services had memory or GC problems in production. How did you track it down?
questions.zh: 讲一次你的 Java 服务在线上出内存或 GC 问题的经历。你是怎么定位的？
outline: Symptoms first: latency spikes or an out-of-memory crash, and when it started
Took a heap dump and looked at what was holding references
Found the cause: an unbounded cache keeping objects alive
The fix: bounded the cache and reduced object churn
Afterwards: GC logging and alerts so it would not come back quietly
followUps: How did you tell it was a leak and not just a small heap?

questions.prompt: Describe a concurrency bug you had to hunt down in Java. What was the root cause?
questions.zh: 讲一个你排查过的 Java 并发 bug。根本原因是什么？
outline: The symptom: wrong counts or timeouts that only showed up under load
It never reproduced locally, so I worked from thread dumps and logs
Root cause: a check-then-act sequence on shared mutable state
The fix: an atomic operation and a smaller critical section
Added a stress test so the race would fail in CI, not in production

chunks.zh: 先检查再执行（一种典型的竞态写法）

followUps: Why not just synchronize the whole method?

questions.prompt: How do declarative transactions work in Spring — and when do they silently stop working?
questions.zh: Spring 的声明式事务是怎么工作的？什么时候会悄悄失效？
outline: Transactions are applied by a proxy around the bean
Self-invocation bypasses the proxy, so the annotation does nothing
Propagation decides whether to join or start a transaction
Rollback happens for runtime exceptions, not checked ones, by default
How I verify: an integration test that forces a failure mid-way
followUps: What happens if the method is private or final?

questions.prompt: How would you find and fix an N+1 query problem in a Java service?
questions.zh: 你怎么发现并修复 Java 服务里的 N+1 查询问题？
outline: Start from the symptom: one slow endpoint, database under pressure
Count the queries for a single request; lazy loading is usually the trigger
Fix options: fetch join, eager loading where it fits, or batch fetching
Watch the connection pool while verifying the fix
Prove it with before-and-after query counts, not just timings

chunks.zh: 懒加载（用到时才查关联数据）
抓取连接（一条 SQL 把关联数据一起查出来）
急加载（查主对象时把关联数据一起查出来）

followUps: When would you keep lazy loading on purpose?

questions.prompt: One of your Java endpoints is too slow. Walk me through how you would profile and speed it up.
questions.zh: 你的一个 Java 接口太慢了。带我过一遍你会怎么剖析和优化。
outline: Measure first: timings per layer before changing anything
Attach a profiler and find the hot path
Common findings: allocation churn from short-lived objects, lock contention, slow queries
Remember benchmarks lie before the JVM has warmed up
Change one thing at a time and re-measure

chunks.zh: 短命对象（很快就变成垃圾的对象）

followUps: How do you make sure the fix did not just move the bottleneck?

questions.prompt: Explain the Java memory model. Why can one thread spin forever on a plain boolean flag set by another thread?
questions.zh: 讲讲 Java 内存模型。为什么一个线程会永远等不到另一个线程设置的普通 boolean 标志？
outline: The symptom: the worker thread never sees the flag change
Threads may cache values; visibility is not automatic
A volatile field creates the happens-before edge that publishes the write
Synchronized and atomics add atomicity on top of visibility
My rule: shared mutable state always gets a concurrent tool

chunks.zh: 用那个保证多线程可见性的关键字修饰的字段
先于关系（事件间的因果先后）

questions.prompt: Which thread-safe building blocks do you actually reach for in Java, and where do they still fail you?
questions.zh: 你在 Java 里实际会用哪些线程安全的构件？它们又会在哪里让你翻车？
outline: Start from the failure: a plain map corrupting under concurrent writes
Atomic classes fix single variables; locks fix compound actions
The trap is check-then-act split across two safe calls
Compare-and-swap loops handle contention without a lock
Contention, not correctness, becomes the ceiling under load

chunks.zh: 先检查再执行（一种典型的竞态写法）
比较并交换（CAS 的全称）

followUps: How do you prove a fix under load, not just in a unit test?

questions.prompt: How do you size a thread pool for a service, and what should happen when its queue is full?
questions.zh: 你怎么给服务定线程池大小？队列满了应该发生什么？
outline: CPU-bound work stays near core count; IO-bound can go higher
Measure wait versus compute before copying numbers from a blog
An unbounded queue hides overload until latency explodes
Full queue is a signal: reject fast or push back on callers
We watch queue depth and task wait time, not just active threads

chunks.zh: 任务队列（跑后台任务用的，t 开头）

followUps: Tell me about a pool setting that caused an incident.

questions.prompt: What problem do virtual threads solve, and where do they not help?
questions.zh: 虚拟线程解决什么问题？又在哪些地方帮不上忙？
outline: Platform threads carry roughly a megabyte of stack each
Virtual threads make blocking style cheap enough to keep
They shine on IO-bound services with thousands of open requests
CPU-bound work gains nothing; the cores are the same cores
Watch out: some blocking paths can still pin the carrier thread

chunks.zh: 平台线程（和虚拟线程相对）
Java 8 引入的可组合异步结果类（C 开头）

followUps: How would you roll virtual threads into an existing service safely?

questions.prompt: Explain type erasure to me. What does it forbid, and how does it bite in real code?
questions.zh: 给我讲讲类型擦除。它禁止了什么？在真实代码里怎么咬人？
outline: Generics are largely a compile-time story; the runtime sees raw types
Erasure is why you cannot create an array of a type parameter
Bounded wildcards express variance the compiler can check
Raw types compile with warnings and defer errors to runtime
Frameworks recover type info through reflection tricks and tokens

chunks.zh: 原始类型（不带类型参数的泛型类）

followUps: How does erasure affect the JSON libraries you use?

questions.prompt: One of your Java endpoints suddenly gets fifty times the traffic. Walk me through how you keep it alive.
questions.zh: 你的某个 Java 接口突然来了五十倍流量。带我走一遍你怎么保住它。
outline: Protect first: rate limiting at the edge before the code suffers
Cache the hot read path and make every write idempotent
Move slow work onto a queue so requests return quickly
Watch the connection pool; the database usually breaks first
Add a circuit breaker so a dying dependency fails fast
followUps: Which metric tells you the service is actually recovering?

questions.prompt: Walk me through a Spring Boot app from startup to the first request it serves.
questions.zh: 带我走一遍 Spring Boot 应用从启动到处理第一个请求的全过程。
outline: The application context refreshes and collects bean definitions
Beans are created, constructor injection wires the graph
Post-processors and auto-configuration shape the final context
Only then does the embedded server open its port
Knowing this order is how I debug works-after-restart mysteries

chunks.zh: 应用上下文（Spring 的容器）
Spring 托管对象的生命周期

followUps: Where do you hook in fail-fast startup checks?

questions.prompt: Streams look clean, but where have they bitten you in production code?
questions.zh: Stream 写起来干净，但在生产代码里它在哪里坑过你？
outline: A stream over a huge result can pull everything into memory
Side effects inside pipeline steps make failures hard to trace
The terminal operation is where the cost actually lands
Short-circuiting saves you only if the pipeline is ordered right
My rule: streams for transformation, loops for control flow

chunks.zh: 流式处理流水线（一串链式操作）

followUps: When is a plain loop honestly the better answer?

questions.prompt: How do you design exception handling across a Java service so errors stay useful?
questions.zh: 你怎么设计一个 Java 服务的异常处理，让错误信息保持有用？
outline: Separate business errors from system failures at the boundary
Never swallow an exception silently; log it or translate it
Transactions decide rollback based on what escapes, so be deliberate
Return an empty Optional only when absence is a normal answer
One global handler keeps the error shape consistent for callers

chunks.zh: 返回一个表示“没有值”的包装对象

followUps: Tell me about an exception you deleted instead of handling.

questions.prompt: Tell me about upgrading a Java service to a newer JDK. What actually breaks?
questions.zh: 讲讲把 Java 服务升级到新版 JDK 的经历。真正会坏的是什么？
outline: The build breaks first: plugins and agents lag the JDK
Dependency conflicts surface through transitive dependencies
Old libraries fall off the classpath or hit removed APIs
GC defaults change, so inherited flags can quietly hurt
We warmed up the new version in staging before trusting it
followUps: Which newer Java feature changed your daily code the most?
